title: Scaling Laws Roadmap
rule: A feature is SHIPPED only when it is complete, stable and no longer needs a roadmap disclaimer.

lanes.label: Next
lanes.description: Approved work after the current line.

statuses.label: Foundation
statuses.description: The rules/data exist, but the player-facing flow is incomplete.

statuses.label: Polish
statuses.description: Working and mostly shaped; needs stabilization or visual/UX pass.

statuses.label: Shipped
statuses.description: 101% rule: complete, stable and safe to check off.

categories.label: Foundation
categories.description: The rules that keep every campaign reproducible, saveable and testable.

items.title: Deterministic campaign clock
items.description: Campaign time advances through one GameDate timeline beginning on 1 January 2022.

items.title: One ordered daily simulation tick
items.description: Deliveries, compute, market demand, bills, gates and solvency resolve in a fixed order.

items.title: Saved deterministic random state
items.description: The same seed and the same decisions replay to the same numbers.

items.title: Simulation separated from Unity
items.description: Economics and game rules run without UnityEngine so balance tests do not need a scene.

items.title: Versioned save migrations
items.description: Old save shapes move forward one version at a time instead of being silently rewritten.

items.title: Save sanitization
items.description: Loaded fields are clamped and invalid enum values fall back to legal states.

items.title: Projection honesty flags
items.description: Estimated hardware and rival data stay distinguishable from known reference data.

items.title: Training projection separated from outcome
items.description: A projected capability never becomes a deployed score until the run actually finishes.

items.title: Playability campaign test
items.description: A scripted multi-year company must survive and stay competitive without trivially dominating.

items.title: Cross-catalog consistency tests
items.description: Catalog sweeps catch impossible ranges, dangling references and dead research paths.

items.title: Scene wiring guards
items.description: PlayMode checks protect critical visual references that EditMode simulation tests cannot see.

categories.label: Founder & Company
categories.description: The opening choices that shape cost, research, training and where the company operates.

items.title: Founder creation screen
items.description: Create the person behind the lab before the campaign begins.

items.title: Seven founder skills
items.description: Development, Management, Teamwork, Concept, Software, Data Engineering and Safety.

items.title: Neutral skill baseline at 20
items.description: Ignoring a skill is a real weakness instead of merely skipping a bonus.

items.title: Skill XP from completed work
items.description: Experience is awarded for finished runs, research, upgrades and releases, never for idle time.

items.title: Founder traits with downsides
items.description: Every opening trait trades one advantage against a real cost.

items.title: Company identity choices
items.description: Opening company profiles change starting cash, reputation, data and default pricing.

items.title: Custom company identity
items.description: Name and define the player's own lab rather than taking a preset.

items.title: World region selection
items.description: Choose the region used to navigate the registration map.

items.title: Sixteen registration countries
items.description: Countries differ on hardware access, tax, innovation and local competition.

items.title: Corporate tax on operating profit
items.description: A loss-making company is not punished with tax on turnover.

items.title: Regional hardware price modifier
items.description: Registration changes what owned silicon costs.

items.title: Regional innovation modifier
items.description: Country choice changes research and upgrade timing.

items.title: Local competition modifier
items.description: Registration changes the brand pressure in the market split.

items.title: Founder appearance in the 3D world
items.description: Connect the creator identity to the physical starter home and later offices.

categories.label: Models & Data
categories.description: From a blueprint to a trained model, a shelf decision and a live product.

items.title: Staged model creator
items.description: Build a model through Foundation, Scale, Data, Compute and Review instead of one giant form.

items.title: Live capability projection
items.description: The creator shows how the last change moved projected capability.

items.title: Training-time projection
items.description: The bill is not the only cost. Calendar time is visible before committing the run.

items.title: Training-cost projection
items.description: The creator prices the run against cash on hand before the player commits.

items.title: Scaling-law quality model
items.description: Parameter count and token count feed one Chinchilla-style quality function.

items.title: Compute-optimal training pressure
items.description: Undertraining or overtraining can waste the same compute budget.

items.title: Dataset catalog
items.description: Eight corpora feed the data side of the training plan.

items.title: Dataset blending rule
items.description: Multiple corpora combine through one normalized mechanism.

items.title: Five audience segments
items.description: Consumer, Developer, Enterprise, Creative and Autonomous demand change over time.

items.title: Five model types
items.description: Specialized model types trade broad reach for stronger audience fit and price tolerance.

items.title: Shelf before release
items.description: A finished run becomes a trained model on the shelf, not an automatic launch.

items.title: Manual release timing
items.description: The player chooses when a trained model reaches the market.

items.title: Per-model pricing
items.description: Multiple live models can carry different prices.

items.title: Eleven model traits
items.description: Reasoning, knowledge, coding and other traits are measured against the market par of the day.

items.title: Trait upgrades consume time and compute
items.description: Model maintenance competes with training for the same calendar and infrastructure.

items.title: Production serving descendant factor
items.description: Inference is priced as served descendants rather than the full training artifact.

items.title: Safety stage in model creator
items.description: Make safety an explicit creation-stage decision before training.

items.title: Keep local vs release flow
items.description: A finished run should branch into internal use or public release instead of one fixed path.

items.title: Serving-capacity decision after training
items.description: Choose rented serving capacity or owned infrastructure after deciding to release.

categories.label: Research & Architecture
categories.description: Technology unlocks, in-house architecture work and the calendar cost of getting there.

items.title: Technology tree
items.description: Seventeen nodes gate architectures, data, model types, upgrades and compute tiers.

items.title: Four research eras
items.description: Foundations, scaling, autonomy and the late frontier structure the tree.

items.title: Research prerequisite graph
items.description: Every unlock must be reachable and cannot open before its own prerequisite.

items.title: Calendar gates
items.description: Research cannot be brute-forced purely by having more cash.

items.title: Cash cost on research
items.description: Time is hard to buy, but research still competes for company capital.

items.title: Artificial Superintelligence node
items.description: The end-state node is visible early but intentionally unreachable in the opening years.

items.title: In-house architecture designer
items.description: Create a custom family instead of only adopting a published architecture.

items.title: Five architecture research directions
items.description: Sparsity, throughput, quality-per-parameter, serving cost and reasoning divide programme focus.

items.title: Budget × calendar power model
items.description: More money cannot fully substitute for more time, and more time cannot replace all budget.

items.title: Focus dilution
items.description: A programme chasing every direction makes less depth in each one.

items.title: Architecture outcome variance
items.description: Cheap or rushed research is deliberately less predictable.

items.title: Six custom family slots
items.description: House architectures resolve through the same downstream interfaces as published families.

items.title: Iterate an owned family
items.description: Improve a house family more cheaply and quickly, with diminishing returns.

items.title: Research-era visual polish
items.description: Finish the visual language and card art around the four research eras.

categories.label: Hardware & Compute
categories.description: The current active development line: rent, own, configure, wait and sometimes regret the timing.

items.title: Hardware generation catalog
items.description: Accelerators, host CPUs, node memory and fabric carry launch dates, price, power and capacity data.

items.title: Known vs projected hardware flag
items.description: Future entries can be labelled as projections rather than blended into history.

items.title: Time-based hardware depreciation
items.description: Owned accelerators lose resale value as calendar time passes.

items.title: Successor depreciation
items.description: Meaningful newer parts apply another phased hit after the player's purchase.

items.title: Performance-per-dollar aging index
items.description: The fleet can be compared with what the same money buys today.

items.title: Rented compute in petaflops
items.description: Cloud rental is capacity, not a fragile count of whatever hardware generation happens to be current.

items.title: Cloud hardware availability lag
items.description: Rental availability follows the hardware frontier with a delay.

items.title: Three compute tiers
items.description: Rented cloud, colocated servers and own datacenter form the infrastructure ladder.

items.title: Owned-cluster balance factor
items.description: Accelerators need enough host CPU, memory and fabric to approach their nominal rating.

items.title: Training scaling-efficiency loss
items.description: Large accelerator counts lose efficiency as the fleet scales.

items.title: Inference utilization model
items.description: Serving and training do not pretend to use the same hardware in the same way.

items.title: Hardware purchase screen
items.description: Turn the existing catalog and economics into a player-facing buy flow.

items.title: Hardware sell flow
items.description: Make resale value visible before the player exits an owned batch.

items.title: Server configuration
items.description: Pair accelerators with host CPUs, node memory and fabric instead of buying one magic server score.

items.title: Hardware launch timeline
items.description: Surface generation timing so waiting becomes an explicit decision rather than hidden knowledge.

items.title: Colocation acquisition flow
items.description: Buy owned hardware with lead time before the company is ready for a full datacenter.

items.title: Own-datacenter acquisition flow
items.description: Turn the late compute tier into a real capital and infrastructure commitment.

items.title: Supply ramp after launch
items.description: A new accelerator generation should not become infinitely available on day one.

items.title: Supply squeezes and shortages
items.description: Make availability another reason a technically good purchase can fail operationally.

items.title: Physical server racks
items.description: Owned compute should appear in company spaces instead of living only in a table.

items.title: Datacenter power planning
items.description: Owned infrastructure eventually needs limits beyond purchase price.

items.title: Datacenter cooling constraints
items.description: Cooling becomes a late physical limit if the infrastructure simulation grows deep enough.

categories.label: Rivals & Intelligence
categories.description: Competitors that react to timing, plus information that can cost money and still be wrong.

items.title: Eight rival labs
items.description: The active field is agent-driven rather than one static score table.

items.title: Historical release seed timeline
items.description: Known releases seed the 2022–2026 opening before agents diverge.

items.title: Patient rival waiting
items.description: Some rivals delay a run when better silicon is close to the planned launch window.

items.title: Rival rush response
items.description: A frontier-focused lab can ship early with a quality penalty when the player opens a large gap.

items.title: Rival capability drift
items.description: Competitors improve between releases instead of freezing until the next launch.

items.title: Procedural post-history releases
items.description: After the known timeline ends, rival strategies generate their own cadence.

items.title: Parody rival naming
items.description: Labs remain recognizable as jokes without using real company names.

items.title: Parody rival logo set
items.description: Finish a consistent small-mark system that remains readable at UI scale.

items.title: Three paid intelligence tiers
items.description: Information quality improves with spend without turning into perfect foresight.

items.title: Real accuracy vs stated confidence
items.description: A report can sound more certain than the underlying signal deserves.

items.title: Hardware launch signals
items.description: Intel can surface an upcoming generation before the player has certainty.

items.title: Price-collapse signals
items.description: Intel can warn about a market event that changes hardware economics.

items.title: Supply-squeeze signals
items.description: Intel can warn that availability is about to tighten.

items.title: Rival-holding signals
items.description: Higher-tier intelligence can flag that a competitor may be waiting on purpose.

items.title: Expanded intelligence report UI
items.description: Give evidence, history and uncertainty more room than a single note card.

items.title: Competitor release history view
items.description: Show how each lab actually moved through the campaign, not just where it stands today.

categories.label: Business & Capital
categories.description: Turn model quality into demand, demand into cash and cash into the next dangerous decision.

items.title: Per-model token pricing
items.description: Each live model carries its own price instead of inheriting one company-wide number.

items.title: Free-tier control
items.description: Free access can be used as a deliberate distribution decision.

items.title: Shared market-share model
items.description: The economy and ranking read from the same demand model.

items.title: Capability term in demand
items.description: Better models earn an advantage but do not automatically own the market.

items.title: Brand term in demand
items.description: Reputation changes how equal products split demand.

items.title: Price term in demand
items.description: Price matters independently of capability.

items.title: Model-age term in demand
items.description: A model that nobody replaces gradually becomes stale.

items.title: Audience-segment curves
items.description: Consumer, Developer, Enterprise, Creative and Autonomous markets change size over time.

items.title: Specialist price tolerance
items.description: A narrower model can reach fewer people while selling to an audience that tolerates higher pricing.

items.title: Company marketing programmes
items.description: Marketing spend acts on demand instead of being a decorative button.

items.title: Model launch push
items.description: A release can receive focused marketing rather than only permanent company spend.

items.title: Funding valuation
items.description: Valuation combines frontier proximity, run rate and the sentiment of the year.

items.title: Investor sentiment cycle
items.description: The same company can be priced very differently depending on when it raises.

items.title: Cap table and founder dilution
items.description: Equity rounds permanently change ownership.

items.title: Down-round penalty
items.description: Raising below the previous valuation costs extra equity.

items.title: Debt facilities
items.description: Bridge, venture debt, bond and sovereign compute debt trade dilution for repayment pressure.

items.title: Arrears and default
items.description: Missed payments accumulate before a public default damages standing.

items.title: Ranking board
items.description: Capability, share and brand feed one sorted company board.

items.title: Ranking history
items.description: Track movement through time instead of showing only today's order.

items.title: Contextual market events
items.description: Add discrete events only where they reinforce an existing market mechanism.

categories.label: Office, Staff & World
categories.description: Make company growth visible in rooms, people, cars, buildings and infrastructure.

items.title: 3D starter home
items.description: The opening company site exists as a real orthographic 3D environment.

items.title: Starter living space
items.description: Living room, workspace and bedroom sell the scale of the first company before expansion.

items.title: Garage
items.description: The starter site includes a garage connected to the planned travel flow.

items.title: Starter car
items.description: The first vehicle gives the world-map transition a physical starting point.

items.title: Fixed orthographic camera
items.description: The scene uses a locked 2.5D presentation rather than free camera navigation.

items.title: Room visual-polish pass
items.description: Keep refining props, lighting and composition without changing the core camera.

items.title: Wall hide / transparency
items.description: Remove room obstruction when the founder enters the garage or another hidden space.

items.title: Founder 3D character
items.description: Place the created founder into the physical company view.

items.title: Founder idle animation
items.description: Give the opening scene life without turning movement into simulation authority.

items.title: Founder waypoint walking
items.description: Move between fixed activity points rather than overengineering pathfinding for the camera distance.

items.title: Walk to workstation
items.description: Training and work actions gain a short physical animation at the desk.

items.title: Walk to garage and car
items.description: Travel begins with the founder physically leaving the starter site.

items.title: World / location map
items.description: Turn location selection into a navigable world layer beyond company registration.

items.title: Rent larger offices
items.description: Company growth should require leaving the starter house.

items.title: Office tiers
items.description: Progress through larger spaces instead of one infinitely expanding room.

items.title: Hiring employees
items.description: Add the team layer that turns empty office capacity into useful company capacity.

items.title: Employee skills
items.description: Staff quality should influence work rather than every hire being interchangeable.

items.title: Employee salaries
items.description: Headcount becomes a continuing operating commitment.

items.title: Physical employee desks
items.description: A hire should appear in the space the company is paying for.

items.title: Walking staff
items.description: Employees move between work points to keep larger spaces alive.

items.title: Owned racks populate the office
items.description: The physical view reads the compute pool and shows what the company actually owns.

items.title: Dedicated company HQ
items.description: A late office tier separates the management fantasy from the starter site.

items.title: Dedicated datacenter site
items.description: Owned infrastructure eventually becomes a place rather than only a finance line.

categories.label: Safety & Incidents
categories.description: Safety should be a decision with tail risk, not a virtue stat that only moves brand.

items.title: Founder Safety skill
items.description: Founder creation already changes incident-risk pressure through the skill system.

items.title: Model Safety trait
items.description: Safety is one of the traits measured against the market par of the day.

items.title: Safety brand effect
items.description: Falling behind on safety already affects how a product is received.

items.title: Incident-risk multiplier foundation
items.description: The simulation has the inputs needed to turn weak safety choices into tail risk.

items.title: Safety stage in model creator
items.description: Make safety visible before training instead of burying it in later upgrades.

items.title: Model safety incidents
items.description: A model far below the safety expectation can produce a costly event.

items.title: Reputation damage from incidents
items.description: Incidents should hit standing that took time and money to build.

items.title: Regulatory attention
items.description: Serious safety failures can create pressure outside the normal demand model.

items.title: Incident response decisions
items.description: Give the player a recovery choice rather than only applying an automatic penalty.

categories.label: Interface & Presentation
categories.description: The game needs to stay legible while the simulation gets denser.

items.title: Bottom control HUD
items.description: The main navigation lives in a bottom control bar instead of a wide left rail.

items.title: Day clock dial
items.description: A half-disc shows date and day progress without controlling the simulation rules.

items.title: Pause / X1 / X2 / X3
items.description: Time controls map cleanly onto the whole-day simulation.

items.title: Skip Day
items.description: Run exactly one day and stop, even when the game is paused.

items.title: Unified accent gradient
items.description: Coral, wine and pale violet are treated as one line moving through the interface.

items.title: Bottom category icon set
items.description: Finish the white single-weight icon language across the major screens.

items.title: Skill icon set
items.description: Seven founder-skill icons are already present and being normalized as one family.

items.title: Section banner art
items.description: Research, Business, Funding and other screens share low-contrast panoramic art.

items.title: Responsive UI Toolkit layout
items.description: Creators and panels defend against shrink, wrap and small-window layout faults.

items.title: Tooltip pass
items.description: Move long explanations out of cramped controls without hiding decisions.

items.title: Resolution and scaling pass
items.description: Test the game across the target window and display sizes.

items.title: Accessibility pass
items.description: Review contrast, focus, motion and readability before a public release.

items.title: Audio feedback
items.description: Add restrained confirmation and warning sounds once the interaction language is stable.

items.title: UI motion pass
items.description: Animate state changes only where motion clarifies what changed.

categories.label: Public Build & Release
categories.description: The public footprint around the game: source, website, roadmap, playtests and store pages.

items.title: Public source repository
items.description: The code and engineering notes are visible while the game changes.

items.title: HCK Labs hub
items.description: Scaling Laws has a permanent home beside the other HCK Labs work.

items.title: Scaling Laws landing page
items.description: The public game page separates current systems from planned work.

items.title: Development mechanism page
items.description: The simulation rules and real-world references have their own crawlable technical page.

items.title: Public roadmap
items.description: This page is the living status map and the JSON behind it is the source of truth.

items.title: Roadmap JSON data source
items.description: One structured file drives the roadmap state and can feed other presentation formats.

items.title: Devlog index
items.description: Create a home for build notes that can be indexed outside social platforms.

items.title: Media gallery
items.description: Collect screenshots, room-evolution clips and later trailers in one crawlable place.

items.title: itch.io project page
items.description: Prepare the first game-specific public page and devlog channel.

items.title: IndieDB project page
items.description: Add a second game-specific public footprint with indexed development updates.

items.title: First public playable build
items.description: Move from screenshots and source to something outside testers can actually run.

items.title: Closed playtest loop
items.description: Collect focused feedback before a wider demo.

items.title: Feedback capture
items.description: Give early players one clear place to report friction and balance problems.

items.title: Steam Coming Soon page
items.description: Start collecting wishlists once the visual direction and core loop can sell the game honestly.

items.title: Playable demo
items.description: A public slice of the loop that proves the game beyond screenshots.

items.title: Gameplay trailer
items.description: Cut the strongest in-game stories once the footage can represent the real loop.

items.title: Release candidate
items.description: Freeze the feature line and spend time on bugs, balance and compatibility.

items.title: Commercial release
items.description: Ship when the game is stable enough that the roadmap no longer has to explain away missing fundamentals.
